story.iWant: a centralized recording service with auto-configuration capabilities
story.soThat: Epic 5's simplified recording features have a solid, testable foundation
story.tasks: - Create recording service file and types (AC: 1) - Implement auto-source selection methods (AC: 2, 3) - Define fixed recording configuration (AC: 4) - Create temp directory management (AC: 5) - Implement service method stubs (AC: 6) - Implement comprehensive error handling (AC: 7) - Write integration tests (AC: 8) - Implement logging system (AC: 9) - Create recording state management (AC: 10)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: `recording.service.ts` created in `src/main/services/` with complete TypeScript types
Auto-select primary screen using `desktopCapturer.getSources()` with no user input required
Auto-select default webcam using `navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices()` with fallback logic
Fixed recording configuration constants defined (resolution, framerate, bitrate, webcam positioning)
Temp directory structure created at `os.tmpdir()/chop-shop/recordings/` with error handling
Comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messages for permission denials and device unavailability
Service integration tests verify auto-selection logic without requiring actual devices
Logging implemented with `[Recording]` prefix for all service operations
Recording state management stub in service (tracks `isRecording`, `currentMode`, `outputFiles`)

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Screen & Webcam Capture (Simplified)
doc.snippet: RecordingService handles all recording logic: screen capture, webcam capture, PiP coordination, MediaRecorder management, auto-source selection, temp file storage. Single self-contained service file (~300-400 lines).

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Fixed configuration with screen: 1920x1080 @ 30fps, 8Mbps; webcam: 640x480 @ 30fps, 2.5Mbps, bottom-right, 20% size, circular shape; audio: auto-select microphone with echo cancellation.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: getPrimaryScreen() and getDefaultWebcam() methods auto-select sources with no user choice. startRecording(mode) and stopRecording() manage recording lifecycle.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Must handle macOS screen recording permissions gracefully. Clear user guidance when permissions denied. Validate all file paths. Ensure MediaStream cleanup on stop to release camera/mic.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Log recording start/stop events with mode, duration, file sizes using `[Recording]` prefix. Log all errors with full stack traces and context.

doc.title: Decision Architecture
doc.snippet: Services located at src/main/services/ following singleton pattern like ffmpeg.service.ts and file.service.ts. Main process only, no renderer involvement.

artifact.reason: Reference pattern for service structure, error handling (FFmpegError, FFmpegErrorCode), and TypeScript typing patterns to follow for recording.service.ts
Example of main process service pattern for file operations and error handling
Reference for service that processes media files, similar patterns may apply for recording

node.package: TypeScript definitions for Node.js (os, path, fs modules)

constraints.constraint: Service must live in src/main/services/recording.service.ts per architecture
Follow singleton pattern like existing services (ffmpeg, file, thumbnail)
Main process only - no renderer involvement at this stage
Use Electron's desktopCapturer API (native, no external dependencies)
NO source selector UI - auto-selection only
NO preview positioning controls - fixed bottom-right corner
NO user configuration - smart defaults only
Must handle macOS permission prompts gracefully with clear user guidance
Validate all file paths before writing to prevent directory traversal
Ensure MediaStream cleanup on stop to release camera/mic

interface.name: RecordingOutput
interface.signature: interface RecordingOutput { files: { screen?: {...}, webcam?: {...} }, metadata: {...} }

tests.standards: Unit tests using mocked Electron APIs (desktopCapturer, mediaDevices). Test error paths extensively (permissions, no devices, busy devices). Verify fallback logic without requiring actual hardware. Integration tests for service initialization and configuration.
tests.locations: - src/main/services/recording.service.test.ts - vitest for unit testing with mocked Electron APIs

ideas.idea: Mock desktopCapturer.getSources() to return array of screens, verify first screen is selected
Mock navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices() to return webcams, verify first videoinput selected
Test fallback behavior when no devices available
Verify RECORDING_DEFAULTS structure matches tech spec (resolution, framerate, bitrate values)
Test temp directory creation with fs.mkdir, verify path format and error handling
Test error handling for NotAllowedError (permissions denied), NotFoundError (no devices), NotReadableError (device busy)
Integration test: initialize service, call getPrimaryScreen and getDefaultWebcam, verify no errors with mocked APIs
